Backend.description: The backend that makes the network real. Only the Kernel backend exists in release 0.1.

oneOf.description: The backend is chosen by the tool: the Kernel backend in release 0.1.
Network namespaces, virtual Ethernet pairs and `netem`.

Change.description: What `set` changes, for each direction. `both` changes the two directions.

both.description: A change of the impairments in both directions.

forward.description: A change of the impairments from the first node to the second.

reverse.description: A change of the impairments from the second node to the first.

env.description: Environment variables besides `NETSCENARIO_*`. Values may use `{node.addr}`.

kind.description: `command`: a program of your own in a node.

ready.description: How the run learns that the program can be used.

run.description:
The program and its arguments, without a shell. `{node.addr}` is replaced by the address of a node;
a brace that is meant as a brace is written twice.

Direction.description: The side of a link that an event acts on.

oneOf.description: From the first node of `between` to the second.
From the second node to the first.

Duration.description: A length of time: a number and a unit (ns, us, ms, s, m, h), a whole number of nanoseconds.

Event.description:
One event of the timeline: at a moment, one thing happens to a link. It does exactly one of `set`,
`outage`, `down` and `up`.

A `set`, a `down` and an `up` are applied before the first packet that its workload sends at or after the moment
(D-038), so the same seed gives the same lost packets; an `outage` is placed by the clock (D-064). Events at the
same moment are applied in the order of the file.

at.description: The moment, from the start of the measured phase. Before the end of it.

direction.description: For an `outage`: the direction it acts on. Both by default.

down.description: The interface of the link goes down: the sender gets errors (D-039).

outage.description:
Nothing is delivered for this long, not even a packet that is on its way, and the sender notices nothing
(D-039, D-064). It is a window in the time of the receiver: from this moment on, for this long, nothing
leaves the link. It does not change the values of the link, which act as before, and the packets that
reach the end of the link in the window are lost.

set.description:
Changes values of the link from this moment on. A key that is not written stays as it is, and `null`
takes the impairment away (the rule of a JSON merge patch).

up.description: The interface of the link comes up again.

FormatVersion.description: The version of the scenario format. Version 0 is the series before 1.0 and may change in any minor release.

Impairments.description: What a direction of a link does to the packets. Everything that is not set is not impaired.

corrupt.description:
The chance that one bit of a packet is flipped (`netem corrupt`). A receiver with the UDP checksum
on drops the packet (D-040).

duplicate.description: The chance that a packet is sent twice (`netem duplicate`). The copy is impaired on its own.

loss.description: Packet loss: independent, or in bursts.

rate.description: A limit on the data rate (`netem rate`).

reorder.description:
Packets that are sent on at once while the others are held back for the delay (`netem reorder`).
Needs `delay`.

ImpairmentsChange.description:
A change of the impairments of one direction. For each key: not written, the value stays; a value, it is
replaced as a whole (a `loss` replaces the loss, it does not merge into it); `null`, the impairment is
taken away. The result must be a valid set of impairments (a `jitter` needs a `delay`), and the reader
checks it for every step.

amount.description:
How much the delay varies: the delay lies within this amount above and below the fixed delay
(`uniform`) or has this standard deviation (`normal`).

JitterDistribution.description: The distribution of the variation of the delay.

oneOf.description: Every delay between delay minus amount and delay plus amount is equally likely.
A bell curve around the delay, cut at about four standard deviations.

Link.description: A link between two nodes, with the impairments of each direction.

between.description: The two nodes. `forward` is the direction from the first to the second.

both.description: The same impairments in both directions. Cannot be combined with `forward` or `reverse`.

forward.description: The impairments from the first node to the second.

reverse.description: The impairments from the second node to the first.

Loss.description:
Packet loss. The model is chosen by `model`, and the parameters are those of `netem`, without aliases
(D-048).

It is read by hand (see `LossFields`), not by a derived reader for a tagged enum: that one collects the
mapping first, and an error in a value is then reported at the start of the mapping and not at the value.

oneOf.description: Every packet is lost with the same chance, independent of the others (`netem loss random`).

p.description: The chance that a packet is lost.

oneOf.description:
Two states, a good and a bad one, with a loss in each (`netem loss gemodel p r 1-h 1-k`). The mean
time in the bad state is `1 / r` packets. All four are required: a missing value would be a default
of `tc` that the file does not show.

loss-bad.description: The chance that a packet is lost while in the bad state (the third argument of `gemodel`).

loss-good.description: The chance that a packet is lost while in the good state (the fourth argument of `gemodel`).

p.description: The chance, for each packet, to go from the good to the bad state.

r.description: The chance, for each packet, to go from the bad to the good state.

oneOf.description:
Four states (`netem loss state p13 p31 p32 p23 p14`): 1 receiving in a gap, 2 receiving inside a
burst, 3 losing inside a burst, 4 losing a single packet in a gap. The numbers are the transitions
between the states they name. From state 1 the chances of `p13` and `p14` add up, and from state 3
those of `p31` and `p32`; neither sum may be above 100 %.

Name.description: A name of 1 to 32 characters: lower case letters, digits and '-', starting with a letter and not ending with '-'.

Probability.description: A probability from 0% to 100% with at most six digits after the point. Always with the percent sign.

Rate.description: A data rate in bits per second, greater than zero: a number and a decimal unit (bit, kbit, mbit, gbit, tbit).

Ready.description:
How the run learns that a program is ready: exactly one of the five ways. The first four need `within`,
the time after which a program that is not ready counts as failed.

delay.description: Ready after this time, whatever the program does. The one way that checks nothing.

file.description: This file exists, a path relative to the directory of the scenario file.

stdout-line.description: A line of the standard output of the program contains this text.

tcp-port.description: A TCP socket listens in the node (read from `/proc/net/tcp`).

udp-port.description: A UDP socket is bound in the node, to any address or to its own (read from `/proc/net/udp`).

within.description: How long to wait for the program to become ready.

Reorder.description:
Reordering by holding packets back (`netem reorder P gap G`).

With a `delay`, a share of the packets is sent on at once and the others wait for the delay, so the ones
that wait arrive after later packets. Measured in D-048: `share` is the share sent on at once, and with
`gap` it is `1 / (gap - 1 + 1 / share)`.

gap.description:
After a packet that was sent on at once, the next `gap - 1` packets are held back before another one
can be sent on at once; 1 (the default) means no such rule. At least 1.

share.description: The chance that a packet is sent on at once.

Shutdown.description:
How a program is stopped at the end of the run: the signal goes to its process group, and `KILL` follows
when it is still there after `within`.

within.description: How long the program has to end. 5 seconds by default.

Signal.description: A signal that asks a program to end. `KILL` is not among them: it is what follows when they do not work.

Size.description: An amount of data in bytes: a number and a unit (b, kb, mb, gb decimal; kib, mib, gib binary), a whole number of bytes.

Topology.description: The nodes and the links. In release 0.1: two nodes and one link (point to point).

id.description: The name of the workload. Metrics are named after it.

kind.description: `udp-cbr`: UDP at a constant bit rate.

start.description: When the workload starts, from the start of the measured phase. Default `0s`.

stop.description: When the workload stops. Default: the end of the measured phase.

udp-checksum.description:
`false`: the packets are sent without the UDP checksum and carry a CRC-32, so a corrupted packet
arrives and is counted as `corrupted` (D-040). Default `true`.

UdpChecksum.description:
Whether the packets of a [`UdpCbr`] carry a UDP checksum.

With the checksum on (the default) a receiver drops a packet whose bits were flipped on the way, as on a
real network. With it off the damaged packet arrives, and the result counts it as `corrupted` (D-040).

In a file it is a boolean, `udp-checksum: false`, and not the words `on` and `off`: YAML 1.1 reads those as
booleans (`PyYAML`, `yamllint` and some editors do), YAML 1.2 as text, and a file must mean one thing in both.

anyOf.description: UDP at a constant bit rate.
A program of your own, started in a node.

Workload.description:
A workload: something that runs in a node. Either a generator that sends traffic ([`UdpCbr`]), or the
program that is being tested ([`Command`]).

It is read by hand (see `WorkloadFields`) for the reason that `Loss` is: the derived reader for a tagged
enum reports an error in a value at the start of the mapping and not at the value.

description: A scenario: a network, what runs in it, and for how long.

duration.description: The length of the measured phase, from the start of the workloads. Greater than zero.

name.description: The name of the scenario. Appears in the result and names its files.

seed.description:
The seed from which the seeds of all random parts are derived. Without it the tool draws one and
records it in the result.

timeline.description: Changes over time: events at moments of the measured phase. Empty if the network stays as it is.

topology.description: The nodes and the link between them.

workloads.description: What sends traffic. At least one.
